who: Charles Edward Timberlake, historian of Russia at Missouri, 1967–2004; PhD Washington, 1968.

evidence.says: University Archives identifies Charles Edward Timberlake, his Washington PhD in 1968, and his Missouri history teaching from 1967 to 2004.
LC identifies Charles E. Timberlake as an assistant professor of history at Missouri, Columbia, and cites Essays on Russian Liberalism (1972).

notes: Institution, period, field and doctorate agree with the supervisor record.

who: Evelyn Bernette Ackerman, historian of modern France and medicine at Lehman College and the CUNY Graduate Center; PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: CUNY lists Ackerman as a history professor affiliated with Lehman, with a Harvard PhD; publications include Village on the Seine and Health Care in the Parisian Countryside.
The faculty list names Evelyn B. Ackerman as professor of history with MA and PhD degrees from Harvard.
LC identifies Evelyn Bernette Ackerman as a Lehman College history professor and author of Village on the Seine and the 1990 French health-care study.
The other Evelyn Ackerman authority describes an artist and designer, with works on antique toys.

notes: The full-name authority matches the CUNY historian through affiliation, degree and publications; the other Evelyn authority is a different person.

who: Louis Lee Woods II, historian of African American history and housing policy at Middle Tennessee State; PhD Howard, 2006.

evidence.says: MTSU identifies Louis Lee Woods II as a history professor with a Howard PhD in 2006 and expertise in civil rights and federal housing policy.
Torren Gatson's May 2018 dissertation names Louis L. Woods as dissertation committee chair.
L. Shelton Woods is a Southeast Asian historian at Boise State with a UCLA PhD.
L. Curry Woods is Lewis Curry Woods III, associated with Culture of Striped Bass and Its Hybrids.
L. C. Woods is Leslie Colin Woods, an Oxford mathematician and author of The Theory of Subsonic Plane Flow.
L. Milton Woods is Lawrence Milton Woods, author of Sometimes the Books Froze and Alex Swan and the Swan Companies.
Louis Woods is an ETH Zurich computer scientist, with computer science degrees in 2008 and 2009 and a dissertation on FPGA data processing.
Louise Woods is a singer and theatre performer.
Louise Woods is the author of Practical Print Making (1996).

notes: The supervisor is directly identified by the student's dissertation. The seven candidates have different full names, fields, works or training; none matches Louis Lee Woods II.

who: Jeffrey R. Yost, historian of computing at Minnesota's Charles Babbage Institute; PhD Case Western Reserve, 1998.

evidence.says: Yost's institutional CV lists a 1998 Case Western Reserve PhD, Minnesota appointments since 1998, HSTM faculty membership since 2010, and coauthorship of FastLane (2016).
LC's Fastlane source note identifies Jeffrey R. Yost as Minnesota HSTM faculty and associate director of the Charles Babbage Institute.

notes: Authority affiliation, program and publication match the institutional CV; doctorate and period agree with AHA.

who: Sara Alpern, historian of US women at Texas A&M; PhD Maryland, 1978.

evidence.says: Alpern's university CV lists a Maryland history PhD in 1978, Texas A&M appointments from 1977 through 2017, and Freda Kirchwey: A Woman of The Nation.
Rachel Michelle Gunter's August 2017 history dissertation names Sara Alpern as committee chair.
LC cites Freda Kirchwey, a Woman of the Nation and identifies Sara Alpern as a Texas A&M history professor.

notes: Direct student evidence, authority affiliation, publication and doctorate agree.

who: Jay Pascal Anglin, historian at Southern Mississippi specializing in early modern England; doctorate UCLA, 1965.

evidence.says: LC records Jay P. Anglin as a variant of Jay Pascal Anglin and identifies him with Southern Mississippi in World History to 1648.
The 1985 society newsletter lists Jay Anglin, program chair, at Southern Mississippi's history department.
AHA lists Jay P. Anglin's UCLA dissertation, The Court of the Archdeacon of Essex, 1571–1609: An Institutional and Social Study, for June 1965.
Southern Mississippi's history faculty bibliography lists Jay Pascal Anglin's Wills of the Archdeaconry of Suffolk, 1620–1624.

notes: The authority's full name and university agree with departmental publications and a contemporary affiliation; UCLA and year match AHA.

who: Muriel Atkin, historian of Russia and Central Asia at George Washington; PhD Yale, 1976.

evidence.says: GW's history profile gives a Yale PhD in 1976, Russian and Central Asian research and courses, and the book Russia and Iran, 1780–1828.
LC identifies Muriel Atkin as a history professor and author of Russia and Iran, 1780–1828 and The Subtlest Battle.

notes: Publication identity, field, university and doctorate agree. LC's earlier Texas at San Antonio affiliation concerns the 1980 publication.

who: Renato Barahona, historian of Spain and early modern Europe at the University of Illinois Chicago, retired 2010.

evidence.says: UIC states that Barahona taught Spanish and early modern European history until 2010; lists Vizcaya on the Eve of Carlism and Sex Crimes, Honour and the Law in Early Modern Spain.
LC identifies the author of those same two books as Renato Barahona, a professor at the University of Illinois Chicago.
Barahona's 1983 article cites his unpublished The Making of Carlism in Vizcaya (1814–1833), Princeton, 1979.

notes: The authority and university profile identify the same UIC historian through affiliation and two books; field and period fit the student's dissertation.
